kf: **Solar lentigines** ('liver spots', 'age spots') are flat, well-defined brown macules on sun-exposed skin.
Face, backs of hands, forearms and shoulders in middle-aged and older adults; a marker of sun damage.
Dermoscopy: fine reticular pattern, 'moth-eaten' edges, fingerprint pattern.
Differentiate from **lentigo maligna** (irregular, enlarging, multiple colours on the face) and pigmented AK or SK.
Benign: sun protection; cryotherapy or laser are cosmetic options.

sub: Over 90% of fair-skinned people over 60; increase with age and sun exposure.

aet: Chronic UV exposure; PUVA and sunbeds produce similar lentigines.
myths: **"They're harmless so never need checking"**: a changing, irregular facial lentigo may be lentigo maligna.
patho_lead: UV causes a **local increase in melanocytes** and pigment along the basal layer.

mech.t: Repeated UV exposure stimulates basal melanocytes.
Melanocyte numbers increase modestly along the basal layer (no nests).
Rete ridges lengthen and are heavily pigmented, creating a flat brown patch.

histo: Elongated, club-shaped, pigmented rete ridges with a slight increase in single basal melanocytes; no atypia.

sub: Asymmetric pigmentation, multiple colours, grey dots, enlargement: refer via the suspected cancer pathway.

comp: Cosmetic concern; may evolve into a flat seborrhoeic keratosis (reticulated SK).
prog: Persist and increase; fade slightly with strict sun protection.
